newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump, seen continuing bull run.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump, seen continuing bull run.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped on Thursday amid a strong rise in turnover as investors kept snapping up shares of newly privatised companies, and traders said the market was likely to continue its recent bull run.
"Today's turnover could have been even higher if the supply of shares would not be limited because many share-owners refuse to sell in expectation of further growth," one broker said.
He added he expected the advance to continue for at least another week.
Turnover jumped to 799.1 million tolars from 338.2 million.
Bank SKB led the day's gainers, leaping 12.52 percent to 41,080 tolars on volume of 6,785 shares.
"SKB probably jumped because of rumours that it may list its shares on the London Stock Exchange," Andrej Potocnik, a trader at brokerage BPH said. SKB has neither confirmed nor denied the rumours.
The seven-share SBI blue chip index rose 47.57 points or 4.01 percent to close at 1,234.16.
Overall, 12 shares rose and five fell, while seven were untraded.
Drug company Lek's new issue "A" shares had highest turnover, firming 6.06 percent to 21,000 tolars on volume of 13,831 shares for total turnover of 288.8 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, falling 10.23 percent to 7,900 tolars on volume of 163 shares for total turnover of 1.3 million tolars.
